# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**Re:** Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)
**Member:** Riley Grant
**Member ID:** W485404613
**Plan:** CountyCare (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Denial date:** 2026-08-09
**Reference number:** POC-5767D9118E-71989
**Governing policy:** EVH CG 2734.CC Outpatient Major Joint Arthroplasty (Hips and Knees) — https://countycare.com/wp-content/uploads/ECG_2734.CC-for-Outpatient-Major-Joint-Arthroplasy-Hips-and-Knees-ver-Dec-25.pdf

Dear CountyCare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which CountyCare denied in the notice dated 2026-08-09 (reference number POC-5767D9118E-71989). The stated reason was that the imaging findings I submitted do not support medical necessity. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I am asking CountyCare to reconsider this decision.

## The Plan's Own Criteria Are Met by My Records

CountyCare's policy states:

> "Replacement/revision of previous arthroplasty Replacement/revision TKA or THA may be considered necessary as an inpatient procedure when the following criteria are met:"

> "● Effusions ● Acute fracture ● Avascular necrosis ● Joint space narrowing or large osteophytes on imaging ● Severe sclerosis or deformity ● Bone on bone contact WITH At least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (6,16,17):"

My records show findings that fall within this list. My MRI dated 2026-05-30 documented full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. On exam, provocative testing was positive on the affected side, and my range of motion was limited by pain. These are the type of imaging and exam findings the plan's own criteria identify: joint space narrowing on imaging, and bone-on-bone contact.

My records also document non-surgical treatment well beyond the 12-week threshold the policy sets out. I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-05-15 through 2026-07-10) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. In addition, I was treated with NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this non-surgical treatment period substantially exceeds the 12 weeks referenced in the plan's criteria.

I understand the policy also includes a section on limitations for outpatient TKA or THA:

> "LIMITATIONS FOR OUTPATIENT TKA OR THA The following criteria deems outpatient TKA or THA as not appropriate:"

The specific limiting criteria under that heading were not provided to me in the denial notice, and I am not able to address bullet points I have not seen. I am requesting that CountyCare identify which, if any, of those specific limitations it believes apply to my case, so that my surgeon and I can respond directly.

The policy also states that where a specific clinical indication is not directly addressed, "medical necessity determination will be made based on widely accepted standard of care criteria," and that the plan's guideline criteria are "developed utilizing evidence-based and peer-reviewed resources from medical publications and societal organization guidelines as well as from widely accepted standard of care, best practice recommendations." My surgeon's documentation reflects 9 months of progressive, unrelieved knee pain; functional limitations including inability to climb stairs without assistance and nighttime pain waking me 3-4 times per night; and imaging and exam findings consistent with advanced degenerative disease. I ask that this be considered under that standard-of-care framework as well.

## Request for the Specific Criteria Applied

I understand that CountyCare may use InterQual criteria, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document, to review requests like mine. I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text that was applied to my determination. I understand I have a right to this information under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules.

## Deadline and Submission

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is not readily available to CountyCare's reviewers, I ask that this be forwarded to the correct department, or I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

## Closing Request

I am asking CountyCare to reconsider this denial in light of the records described above and the plan's own published criteria, and to provide the specific InterQual criteria applied to my case. Please let me know if any additional documentation from my surgeon would help this review. Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Riley Grant]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W485404613

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
